deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 64 is a page of lecture or study notes on ancient Greek history, written in German Kurrent script. It continues directly from the previous page, which narrates Athenian history from Solon through the Peisistratids to about 500 BC.

Lines 1–2 finish that narrative: in 500 BC the Athenians took part in the revolt of the Asiatic Greeks (the Ionian Revolt) and helped burn Sardis.

The page then opens a new section, '2, Geschichte der griechischen Kolonien' (History of the Greek colonies). It argues that no ancient people founded as many colonies as the Greeks, and that these colonies mattered for Greece and for world history, for three reasons:
(a) The colonies were ahead of the mother country in culture, and through continued contact this culture flowed back into Greece.
(b) Many colonies became important through trade. The cities of mainland Greece never became such great trading cities; the colonies carried on a large world trade.
(c) Some colonies became powerful enough to have great influence on political history.

The notes then limit the topic to colonies founded by Hellenes between the Dorian migration and Alexander the Great. These colonies spread around the shores of the Mediterranean, Aegean and Black Seas. The next page continues with the colonies of Asia Minor (Aeolian, Ionian, Dorian).

The content and structure (the a/b/c scheme of the importance of colonies, the emphasis on trade and 'Welthandel') closely match the Göttingen ancient-history lectures in the tradition of A. H. L. Heeren. The page is most likely student or family lecture notes kept in the Gauss papers, not Gauss's own mathematical work. Nothing mathematical can be reconstructed.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no derivations to check.

Historical note: the dates on the adjacent pages (e.g. Aeolian colonization c. 1124, Ionian migration c. 1044) follow the traditional chronology used in early-19th-century textbooks; they are not errors of this page.

transcription_corrections: Line 1: the opening reads more like 'sie Theil an dem Aufstand' (an insertion mark sits before 'Theil'), continuing '500 nahmen' from the previous page. 'den Theil' is likely a misreading.

In the sentence on trade, 'keinen[?] großen Welthandel' is doubtful. The logic contrasts mainland cities, which never became great trading cities, with colonies that 'trieben zum Theil einen ... großen Welthandel', so the word is probably 'einen' plus an adjective, not 'keinen'.

The sentence 'Doch nichts bildeten sie sich mehr als wenn sie Kolonien aus sich ...' is heavily corrected and largely illegible. The interlinear word read as 'Verlust' is uncertain (possibly 'Verkehr'), and 'Glieder' may be 'Gliedern' / 'bildeten'. Treat this whole passage as conjectural.

A cross-reference mark '†††' appears after 'dorischen' and again near the end ('mittelländischen, [-Meers-] ††† ägeischen und schwarzen Meers'). The machine transcription drops it; it marks an insertion or revision.
The page number '64' is written in the top left corner.
